There's an issue with your API key — malformed, revoked, or expired
Your request body exceeded the size limit
You've hit a rate limit
questions.explain: 401 authentication_error specifically means a problem with the API key itself, not the request body or usage volume.

questions.q: If a request fails with a 400 invalid_request_error, what should your code do?
options: Retry it once more without changes
Retry it with exponential backoff
Fix the request body — retrying the same malformed request will fail identically every time
Wait for the retry-after header and retry
questions.explain: A 400 means something is wrong with the request itself; resending the exact same request produces the exact same failure.

questions.q: Which of these status codes IS worth retrying with backoff?
options: 404 not_found_error
403 permission_error
401 authentication_error
529 overloaded_error
questions.explain: 529 overloaded_error is a transient, server-side condition — exactly the kind of error exponential backoff is meant for.

questions.q: What does exponential backoff mean in a retry loop?
options: Retrying immediately, as many times as possible
Waiting progressively longer between each retry attempt (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s)
Giving up after the very first failure
Sending the request to a different API endpoint each time
questions.explain: Exponential backoff increases the wait time between attempts, avoiding hammering a struggling server with immediate retries.

questions.q: What is the request_id field in an error response for?
options: It's a value you'd quote to support when investigating a specific failed request
It must be resent in the next retry attempt
It identifies which model generated the error
It's only present on successful responses
questions.explain: Every response includes a request_id, useful for tracking and debugging a specific request when contacting support.
